questions.question: In the Bradley–Terry model with item scores $w_i$, what is the probability that item $i$ is preferred over item $j$?
questions.choice_A: $\displaystyle \frac{e^{w_i}}{e^{w_i}+e^{w_j}}$
questions.choice_B: $\displaystyle \frac{w_i}{w_i+w_j}$
questions.choice_C: $\displaystyle \sigma(w_i-w_j)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-(w_i-w_j)}}$ with $\sigma$ independent of $w_j$
questions.choice_D: $\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}+\frac{w_i-w_j}{2}$

questions.question: Which best describes the Plackett–Luce model for a full ranking $(i_1 \succ i_2 \succ \dots \succ i_K)$ over a subset of items?
questions.choice_A: It assigns equal probability to all permutations consistent with pairwise BT probabilities.
questions.choice_B: It factorizes the ranking probability into a product of stagewise choice probabilities with softmax over remaining items at each stage.
questions.choice_C: It models only the top-1 choice and ignores lower ranks.
questions.choice_D: It assumes independent pairwise comparisons across all pairs in the list.

questions.question: Why do Bradley–Terry and Plackett–Luce models exhibit an additive identifiability issue in the scores $w$?
questions.choice_A: Because the likelihood depends only on pairwise differences $|w_i-w_j|$.
questions.choice_B: Because probabilities involve products of scores, making them scale-invariant.
questions.choice_C: Because the probabilities depend only on differences $w_i-w_j$ or ratios $e^{w_i}/\sum e^{w_k}$, which are unchanged by adding a constant to all $w$.
questions.choice_D: Because the models require the sum of probabilities to be 1.

questions.question: Which normalization constraint is commonly imposed to resolve the additive indeterminacy in BT/PL models?
questions.choice_A: $\sum_i e^{w_i}=1$
questions.choice_B: $\prod_i w_i=1$
questions.choice_D: $\sum_i w_i=0$ or fix one $w_i$ to a reference value

questions.question: What is the log-likelihood contribution of a single observed pairwise win $i \succ j$ under the Bradley–Terry model?
questions.choice_A: $\log \frac{e^{w_i}}{e^{w_i}+e^{w_j}}$
questions.choice_B: $\log \sigma(w_i-w_j)$ where $\sigma$ is any sigmoid
questions.choice_C: $w_i-w_j$
questions.choice_D: $\log \frac{w_i}{w_i+w_j}$

questions.question: Which statement about the score function–probability relationship is correct for these preference models?
questions.choice_A: Probabilities are linear in scores if scores are normalized.
questions.choice_B: Choice probabilities are a softmax over scores: $P(i \text{ chosen from } S)=\exp(w_i)/\sum_{k\in S}\exp(w_k)$.
questions.choice_C: Probabilities depend on $w$ only through $\|w\|_2$.
questions.choice_D: Only differences of squared scores matter.

questions.question: For the Bradley–Terry model, what is the gradient of the log-likelihood with respect to $w_i$?
questions.choice_A: The number of losses of $i$ minus the number of wins of $i$.
questions.choice_B: A constant depending only on the number of items.
questions.choice_C: Wins of $i$ minus the expected wins under the model: $\sum_{j} n_{ij}^{\text{win}} - \sum_j n_{ij} \frac{e^{w_i}}{e^{w_i}+e^{w_j}}$.
questions.choice_D: $\sum_j (w_i-w_j)$ over all opponents $j$.

questions.question: In the Plackett–Luce model, which is a correct expression for the probability of a full ranking $(i_1 \succ i_2 \succ \dots \succ i_K)$ from set $S$?
questions.choice_A: $\prod_{t=1}^{K} \frac{e^{w_{i_t}}}{\sum_{k\in S} e^{w_k}}$
questions.choice_D: $\prod_{t=1}^{K} \frac{e^{w_{i_t}}}{\sum_{k\in S\setminus\{i_1,\dots,i_{t-1}\}} e^{w_k}}$

questions.question: Which condition ensures the maximum likelihood estimates exist and are unique up to an additive constant in the Bradley–Terry model?
questions.choice_A: The comparison graph is strongly connected (every item can reach every other via a path of wins).
questions.choice_B: Each item has at least one win.
questions.choice_C: There are at least as many comparisons as items.
questions.choice_D: The sum of all scores is zero.

questions.question: How does adding an $\ell_2$ regularizer $-(\lambda/2)\|w\|_2^2$ to the log-likelihood affect estimation?
questions.choice_A: It makes the model scale-invariant.
questions.choice_B: It pins down the additive constant, yields a unique solution, and shrinks extreme estimates, improving numerical stability.
questions.choice_C: It enforces sparsity in the scores.
questions.choice_D: It has no effect on identifiability.

questions.question: Which property of BT/PL models explains why additive shifts of all scores do not change predicted probabilities?
questions.choice_A: Homogeneity of degree zero in the exponentiated scores $\{e^{w_i}\}$.
questions.choice_B: Symmetry under permutation of item labels.
questions.choice_C: Invariance of softmax to common additive offsets: $\mathrm{softmax}(w+c)=\mathrm{softmax}(w)$.
questions.choice_D: Orthogonality of score vectors.

questions.question: What is a common computational approach to obtain the MLE for Bradley–Terry parameters?
questions.choice_A: Closed-form solution via eigen-decomposition.
questions.choice_B: Single-pass counting algorithm.
questions.choice_C: Iterative optimization such as Newton–Raphson or gradient ascent on the concave log-likelihood.
questions.choice_D: Greedy stagewise selection.

questions.question: What happens to the Fisher information matrix for BT/PL parameters without a normalization constraint?
questions.choice_A: It is full rank for any dataset with at least one comparison.
questions.choice_B: It becomes rank-deficient by one due to the additive shift invariance.
questions.choice_C: It is diagonal with identical entries.
questions.choice_D: It is undefined because probabilities do not depend on parameters.

questions.question: Which extension allows handling ties in pairwise comparisons beyond the basic Bradley–Terry model?
questions.choice_A: Bradley–Terry–Luce with isotonic constraints.
questions.choice_B: Davidson model, which adds a tie parameter affecting the probability mass at equality.
questions.choice_C: Gumbel–Softmax relaxation.
questions.choice_D: Borda count aggregation.

questions.question: In the Plackett–Luce model, how do partial rankings (e.g., top-$k$ lists) enter the likelihood?
questions.choice_A: Only the top-1 choice contributes; lower ranks are ignored.
questions.choice_B: By marginalizing over unobserved permutations consistent with the observed top-$k$ using the stagewise product up to $k$.
questions.choice_C: By uniformly distributing probability over all missing ranks.
questions.choice_D: They cannot be modeled; PL requires full rankings.

questions.question: Which statement about convexity is correct for estimation in BT and PL models?
questions.choice_A: Both have non-concave log-likelihoods with many local maxima.
questions.choice_B: The negative log-likelihood is convex in $w$ up to an additive constant, enabling reliable global optimization.
questions.choice_C: Convexity holds only if all items have equal sample sizes.
questions.choice_D: Convexity fails when regularization is used.

questions.question: What is a typical gradient term for the Plackett–Luce log-likelihood with respect to $w_i$ across rankings?
questions.choice_A: Count of times $i$ appears minus the number of items.
questions.choice_B: Sum over stages where $i$ is selected of 1 minus the softmax probability of $i$ at that stage; otherwise minus the softmax probability.
questions.choice_C: Sum of differences $w_i-w_j$ over all $j$ that follow $i$.
questions.choice_D: A constant equal to the number of rankings containing $i$.

questions.question: Why can undefeated items cause problems for unregularized MLE in Bradley–Terry?
questions.choice_A: They violate the independence of irrelevant alternatives.
questions.choice_B: They make the likelihood unbounded, pushing the corresponding $w_i\to +\infty$ without a finite maximizer.
questions.choice_C: They force all other scores to zero.
questions.choice_D: They make the gradient exactly zero for all parameters.

questions.question: How does the softmax connection arise from a random-utility interpretation of PL?
questions.choice_A: Utilities are Gaussian, leading to probit choice probabilities.
questions.choice_B: Utilities are $w_i$ plus i.i.d. Gumbel noise, yielding multinomial logit (softmax) choice probabilities.
questions.choice_C: Utilities are Cauchy, yielding heavy-tailed softmax.
questions.choice_D: Utilities are Laplace, yielding exponential race with max-linear probabilities.

questions.question: Which practical regularization reflects a Bayesian prior and improves estimation stability in sparse data settings?
questions.choice_A: $\ell_1$ prior on $e^{w_i}$ corresponding to Laplace on $w_i$
questions.choice_B: Gaussian prior on $w_i$ leading to $\ell_2$ penalty on $w$
questions.choice_C: Uniform prior on scores leading to no penalty
questions.choice_D: Jeffreys prior producing hard constraints

questions.question: Which statement best captures the relation between pairwise BT and listwise PL models?
questions.choice_A: PL reduces to BT when $K=2$ by making the stagewise softmax over two items equal to the BT pairwise probability.
questions.choice_B: BT is a special case of PL only when all items have equal scores.
questions.choice_C: BT and PL are incompatible because one is pairwise and the other is listwise.
questions.choice_D: PL can be derived by multiplying independent BT probabilities across all pairs in a ranking.
